newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists want Chirac to sue Le Pen.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists want Chirac to sue Le Pen.

text.p: France's Socialists called on President Jacques Chirac on Monday to sue extreme-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen for saying the president was on the payroll of Jewish organisations.

"In this way, Chirac would have an opportunity to prove his determination...and back his own words when he says he wants to fight racism," Socialist spokesman Francois Hollande told a news conference.

Le Pen, whose National Front (FN) party has just won a fourth town in municipal elections, was quoted on Friday as saying Chirac was "in the grasp...of Jewish organisations and notably the notorious B'nai Brith," a U.S.-based Jewish masonic group.

Hollande was reacting to a speech Chirac made on Sunday to French Jewish leaders in which he criticised opponents of new legislation to curb illegal immigration as "ambiguous, lax and naive." His remarks appeared aimed at Socialist Party leaders.
The explosive illegal immigration issue has fuelled Le Pen's electoral successes.

Hollande said Chirac should also take legal action against Catherine Megret, just elected National Front mayor of the southern town of Vitrolles, who was quoted by a German newspaper last week as saying there were "differences between races."

Le Pen won 15 percent of the vote in the 1995 presidential election. While France's far-right press regularly fulminates against what it sees as a conspiracy of Jews and freemasons, Le Pen's language has usually been more guarded since several explosive statements in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
Chirac spoke to the Jewish leaders on the 190th anniversary of Napoleon's recognition of full civil rights for French Jews.
He used the opportunity to level a strong attack against the FN and reassert his intention to curb illegal immigration.
The day was marred by a potentially embarassing development for Chirac when a message from his wife was read out loud at a meeting of ultra-rightist Catholic fundamentalists.

Abbe Philippe Laguerie read a note signed by Bernadette Chirac's private secretary saying she was pleased to have been invited to a banquet his group was holding but could not attend because she was abroad.
Laguerie, whose past public comments about Moslems and Jews make Le Pen seem moderate in contrast, said the letter quoted Bernadette Chirac as saying she sincerely regretted being unable to attend.

He added that Bernadette Chirac, who is a devout Catholic, attended mass in his church several times before her husband became president in 1995. Chirac himself is not known to be a particularly observant Catholic.
Laguerie, who is on poor terms with French church leaders, is best known for holding memorial masses for such figures as the late convicted Nazi collaborator Paul Touvier.
The president's office said on Monday the note from his wife's office to Laguerie "was just a polite, negative acknowledgement to a letter like thousands she gets each day."
